    Added additional clues in hash_info.html pages

    To help competitors, two additional clues are provided. First, the
    specific size of the hashes are give (Part1: 32-bit; Part2: 64-bit).
    Second, the C language is mentioned specifically to let people know how
    to handle integer overflows.

    Some languages handle numbers differently, particularly in regards to
    calculating numbers larger than the bit-wise limitation. For example, an
    unsigned 32-bit integer has a maximum value of 4294967295. When
    exceeding this value, C will wrap back to 0 while other languages such
    as Python may simply increase the size of the number (then truncate down
    as needed).
